To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Rotavirus infection was diagnosed in young foals in two breeding periods in Greece, 2006 and in 2007.

rotavirus-like particles were found by electron microscopy in faeces of young foals during two consecutive breeding seasons at the same stud-farm and that the rotavirus strains were genetically identical, indicating persistence of the same strain in the stud-farm.

the rotavirus strains that were isolated in the current study were highly similar to those circulating in other countries in Europe and that the virus was persistent in the stud farm for at least two consecutive foaling seasons.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the first report on the molecular characterisation of group A rotavirus strains circulating on Greek stud farms and the first evidence of rotavirus infection in foals in the country.
the molecular characterization of equine rotavirus G3AP[6] and G3AP[8] strains circulating in Greece, the first report of such viruses in this country.
the molecular epidemiology and phylogenetic characterization of equine rotaviruses circulating in Greece, and the possible association of these viruses with the outbreaks of diarrhoea in the foals.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
these outbreaks in Greece are the first report of group A rotavirus infections in horses in the Mediterranean area.
a G3AP[6] rotavirus strain was responsible for the severe diarrhoeic syndrome in foals in a Greek stud farm.
these outbreaks of severe diarrhoea in young foals in Greece were associated with a novel equine rotavirus strain of the G3AP[4] genotype.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the G3AP[4] rotavirus strains circulating at the stud farm in Greece were genetically similar to those recently reported in other European countries and the same strains were responsible for the two consecutive outbreaks of diarrhoea in the foals.
the G3AP[6] rotavirus strain is a common cause of diarrhoeal outbreaks among equids in Greece.
equine rotavirus infection is an important cause of diarrhoea in young foals and the disease is associated with significant morbidity, mortality and economic losses.
The main takeaway from our work is that
equine rotavirus infection can cause a severe diarrhoea in young foals.
rotavirus infections are a common cause of diarrhoea in young horses in Greece and that the viruses are genetically similar to the viruses circulating in Europe.
rotavirus is an important pathogen in young foals, and that the virus may cause severe disease in the absence of concurrent infections with other pathogens.
